sections.heading: 1. Adolescence and Puberty
points: **Adolescence** = the period of life between about **11 and 18/19 years**, of rapid growth and change.
**Puberty** = when the body becomes **capable of reproduction**; it ends when an adolescent reaches reproductive maturity.
Changes are brought about by **hormones** secreted by **endocrine glands**.

sections.heading: 2. Changes at Puberty
points: **Increase in height** (growth spurt); girls usually mature earlier than boys.
**Voice change** — deeper in boys (larynx grows → 'Adam's apple').
**Skin changes** — active oil glands → pimples.
**Development of secondary sexual characters** — e.g. facial hair in boys; development of breasts in girls.
**Mental, emotional and intellectual maturity** also develop.

sections.heading: 3. Hormones and Reproductive Health
points: **Endocrine glands** pour hormones directly into the blood.
Sex hormones: **testosterone** (testes, male), **oestrogen** (ovaries, female).
Other glands/hormones: **pituitary** (master gland), **thyroid (thyroxine, needs iodine)**, **pancreas (insulin — diabetes)**, **adrenals**.
**Menstruation** and the **menstrual cycle** (about 28 days) begin at puberty (menarche) and stop around 45–50 (menopause).

sections.heading: 4. Sex Determination and Health
points: Humans have **sex chromosomes: XX (female), XY (male)**.
The **father's sperm** determines the sex of the child (X → girl, Y → boy) — the **mother is not responsible**.
Adolescents need a **balanced diet** (iron-rich to prevent anaemia), **hygiene**, exercise; and must **avoid drugs/tobacco/alcohol** ('say no to drugs').

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Adolescence ≈ 11–19 years; puberty = capacity to reproduce; driven by hormones.
Sex hormones: testosterone (male), oestrogen (female); pituitary = master gland; thyroxine needs iodine.
Menarche = start of menstruation; menopause ≈ 45–50 years.
Sex chromosomes: XX = girl, XY = boy; the FATHER's sperm decides the child's sex.
Balanced (iron-rich) diet, hygiene; avoid drugs/tobacco/alcohol.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **father** determines the child's sex (the Y-bearing sperm gives a boy) — the mother is never responsible.
**XX = female, XY = male**.
**Testosterone = male**, **oestrogen = female** hormone; **pituitary = master gland**.
**Thyroxine** (thyroid) needs **iodine**; **insulin** (pancreas) controls sugar.
